newsitem.title: FRANCE: Foncier sit-in to end if statutes changed -source.
newsitem.headline: Foncier sit-in to end if statutes changed -source.

text.p: Credit Foncier staff plan to call off their sit-in at the property lender's headquarters on Wednesday if the government agrees at a shareholders' meeting to new statutes giving it more time to repair its balance sheet, a union source said.
An extraordinary shareholders' meeting has been called for later on Wednesday to decide on a technical motion giving the bank up to two years to pull its balance sheet out of the red.
But this does not mean a state plan to dismantle the bank has been shelved and talks are continuing, the source said.

"This will be the last day of our occupation but it does not mean we do not remain mobilised. We are still talking to the (state-appointed) mediator," the source from a cross-union bank negotiating group said, asking not to be identified.

Workers at the severely troubled lending group occupied its Paris headquarters nearly three weeks ago and held the bank's chairman hostage for six days to protest against government plans to split up the assets and wind part of the bank down.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe appointed a mediator in January to discuss the future of Credit Foncier, whose balance sheet plunged an estimated 2.5 billion francs into the red once it had reported a massive 1995 loss last April.

Under the 145-year-old lender's statutes, different from those applying to ordinary companies, Credit Foncier should have plugged its balance sheet within four months and has only stayed in business following a state-sponsored takeover, announced in July and designed to pave the way for a future break-up.
